title: Dynamic TTL laddering recommender and safe apply flow for KV/prefix caching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a conservative, automated recommender that suggests TTL ladders and cache-key normalizations for KV/prefix caches to reduce token cost while bounding risk to latency and correctness. The system uses a lightweight hit-rate emulator (Poisson-sampled request traces + prefix-distillation) to estimate expected hit lift and tail latency under candidate TTL ladders, and generates a staged apply plan with canary cohorts, shadow verification, and an automatic rollback trigger based on business SLOs. This ticket covers the modeling engine, recommender heuristic set, safe apply orchestration and the initial console UI for ops to review suggestions.
acceptance_criteria: Modeling engine ingests sampled request traces and outputs hit-rate delta and expected miss-rate percentile for candidate TTL ladders
Recommender produces an ordered list of up to 5 candidate configurations with expected cost savings and risk score
Safe apply orchestration can run a staged rollout: shadow -> 1% canary -> 10% ramp -> full apply, with automated rollback when miss-rate or 95th P99 latency regressions exceed thresholds
End-to-end integration test that runs on historical traces demonstrates cost savings >= 6% for two internal workloads without exceeding latency SLOs
Console UI shows recommendation rationale, time-series sims, and one-click promote/rollback actions for SREs
notes: Design decision: use Poisson sampling to simulate request inter-arrival for efficiency; avoid heavy simulator that replays full traffic in prod cluster
We will normalize keys by: canonicalizing query args, hashing user-scoped tokens separately, and optionally applying entropy bucketing for noisy prefixes

Risk trade-off: aggressive TTL increases reduce requests to runtime but can hide correctness regressions if keys include ephemeral user state. We will tag recommendations with 'statefulness risk' and require manual approval for high-risk prefixes

Initial heuristics: (1) ladder TTLs in powers-of-two seconds for predictable eviction curves; (2) prefer per-prefix TTL caps rather than global increases; (3) skip rules for keys with high prefix-change rate (>30% per hour)
implementation_plan: M1 (2w): modeling prototype that accepts sampled traces and generates hit-lift & miss-lift metrics
M2 (1w): recommender that scores candidates with cost/risk heuristics and serializes plans
M3 (1w): safe-apply orchestrator with canary gating and metric monitoring hooks
M4 (1w): console integration and documentation + init A/B run on non-critical workload
M5 (ongoing): iterate heuristics and add ML-based ranking when we have 10+ evaluated runs
monitoring_and_gates: Gate-1 (shadow): absolute miss-rate delta <= 0.2% and P99 latency delta <= 2ms
Gate-2 (1% canary): miss-rate delta <= 0.5% and P99 delta <= 5ms
Gate-3 (10% ramp): miss-rate delta <= 1% and P99 delta <= 8ms
Auto-rollback trigger: sustained violation for 3 consecutive 1m windows or >0.5% user-facing error increase
instrumentation_required: Per-key sample trace sink for 1 minute per config run
End-to-end synthetic probe that validates correctness-sensitive keys
Cost estimator that converts miss/lift into expected token-unit savings
